title: Grateful Dead Live at Family Dog at the Great Highway on 1970-03-01
venue: Family Dog at the Great Highway

ai_review.summary: High‑energy 1970 show with a standout Cryptical > Other One sequence and solid mid‑set, captured on mostly soundboard tape though the opening tracks are noisy.
ai_review.review: Fans rave about the intensity of the Cryptical–Other One stretch, the tight Good Lovin' drums, and the beautiful renditions of Black Peter, China Cat → I Know You Rider and Baby Blue. The recording is a 1970 soundboard with audience bleed on the first two songs (and a few seconds later), so the middle of the set sounds clear while the opening and closing fragments are rough and sometimes have vocal‑mix issues.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.25/5; most comments praise the performance and only note moderate recording flaws on early tracks, yielding a strong overall score.

recording_quality.technical_notes: First two songs (and a few seconds of the third) come from audience mics and are muddy; vocals sit high in the mix throughout, requiring EQ for best listening. The middle section is clear and well‑balanced, though some reviewers note occasional harp level spikes.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: A solid Sunday‑night run with a rare ‘Big Boy Pete’ and an exciting Cryptical > Other One transition that mirrors the New Orleans show a month earlier. The set moves smoothly through folk‑rock numbers into bluesy jams, ending with a classic Baby Blue before the tape cuts.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Generally praised for his guitar work; one reviewer notes it could be a touch louder but overall 'great board' of Garcia's playing.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s harmonica receives glowing remarks, though a few note occasional level spikes. Organ/guitar balance on The Other One is mentioned as lacking.
band_member_comments.Drums: Good Lovin' drums highlighted positively; overall rhythm section described as tight.
